final_writeup:
The target is the graceful tree conjecture, explicitly described as open in the permitted source. I do not claim a universal proof or counterexample. The rigorous progress is as follows.

First, every caterpillar is graceful by an explicit formula. Let its spine be v1,...,vk and let Li be the off-spine leaves adjacent to vi. Put odd spine vertices and leaves at even spine vertices in one bipartition class A; order A by scanning the spine and writing vi for odd i and Li for even i. Order the other class B by writing Li for odd i and vi for even i. If x has rank p in A and y rank q in B, label x by p and y by n+1−q. Listing the leaf edges at v1, then v1v2, the leaf edges at v2, then v2v3, and so forth, their endpoint-rank sums are consecutively 2,3,...,n. Their differences are consequently n−1,n−2,...,1.

Second, this construction is not merely proving a disguised stronger conjecture. Let H have center c, three neighbors ui, and one leaf wi adjacent to each ui. The labeling c=1, (u1,w1)=(7,3), (u2,w2)=(6,5), (u3,w3)=(4,2) is graceful. Nevertheless H has no graceful labeling in which one bipartition class lies wholly below the other. The four-case rank argument is recorded below. Thus the natural alpha-labeling approach already fails on this seven-vertex graceful tree.

There is also an infinite non-caterpillar family. Add r≥0 new leaves at c in H and label them 8,9,...,7+r. The original differences are 1,...,6 and the new differences are 7,...,6+r, so the resulting 7+r vertex tree is graceful. Its non-leaf-induced subtree contains a 3-star and hence is not a path.

Finally, the persisted exact checker proves every tree with at most 15 vertices graceful. It generates all unlabeled trees inductively by leaf attachment and removes isomorphic duplicates with a complete center-rooted canonical code. For every representative it constructs a labeling and then independently checks that the labels are exactly 0,...,n−1 and the differences exactly 1,...,n−1. The completed run covered 13,188 representatives.

Consequently, any counterexample to the target must have at least 16 vertices and must contain a vertex adjacent to at least three non-leaves. These results do not settle arbitrary non-caterpillar trees of unbounded order, so the claimed resolution is PARTIAL.

results.claim: Ordered-bipartition criterion: a bipartite n-vertex tree with classes A={x1,...,xa} and B={y1,...,yb} has a bipartition-separated graceful labeling if and only if the two classes can be ordered so that the endpoint-rank sums i+j over edges xiyj are pairwise distinct.
results.proof_sketch: There are n−1 edges and every rank sum lies in {2,...,n}, also of size n−1; hence pairwise distinct sums are exactly 2,...,n. Given such orders, set phi(xi)=i and phi(yj)=n+1−j. These are precisely the labels 1,...,a and a+1,...,n, and the difference on xiyj is n+1−i−j. Thus the differences are exactly 1,...,n−1. Conversely, in a separated labeling the lower class of size a necessarily receives 1,...,a. Order it increasingly and the upper class decreasingly. The same formula expresses every difference as n+1 minus the corresponding endpoint-rank sum, proving the converse.

results.claim: For every caterpillar, the bipartition orders described in the final writeup give endpoint-rank sums 2,3,...,n in succession.
results.proof_sketch: Let Li be the ordered block of off-spine leaves at vi. Traverse the edges as the Li-edges followed, when i<k, by vivi+1, for i=1,...,k. At v1 the varying endpoint occupies the first positions of the opposite bipartition order, so the first sum is 2. Within each leaf block its rank rises by one. The next spine vertex immediately follows that block in the same bipartition order, so the spine-edge sum rises by one as well. After crossing that spine edge, the first leaf at the new spine vertex immediately follows the previous spine vertex in the other class, again increasing the sum by one. Induction gives consecutive sums. There are n−1 edges, so the final sum is n. Empty leaf blocks cause no change to the argument.
For n≤2 this is immediate. Otherwise apply the ordered-bipartition criterion to the orders supplied by the preceding claim. The explicit labeling is phi(xi)=i and phi(yj)=n+1−j.

results.claim: Extreme-vertex leaf-extension lemma: if a graceful n-vertex tree has a vertex v labeled 1, attaching any s≥0 new leaves at v preserves gracefulness.
results.proof_sketch: Keep the old labels and give the new leaves labels n+1,...,n+s. The old edge differences are 1,...,n−1, while the new edges at v have differences n,...,n+s−1. Together these are exactly 1,...,n+s−1. If v originally has label n instead, first complement every label by x↦n+1−x.

results.claim: For every r≥0, the tree obtained from the once-subdivided K1,3 by adjoining r additional leaves to its center is a graceful non-caterpillar.
results.proof_sketch: Let c be the center and let cui, uiwi (i=1,2,3) be the subdivided arms. Assign c=1 and (ui,wi)=(7,3),(6,5),(4,2). The six differences are 6,4,5,1,3,2. Give the r extra center-leaves labels 8,...,7+r; their differences are 7,...,6+r. Thus all required differences occur once. The vertices c,u1,u2,u3 are non-leaves and induce K1,3, not a path, so the tree is not a caterpillar.

results.claim: The once-subdivided K1,3 has no bipartition-separated graceful labeling; hence not every tree admits the stronger alpha-type labeling used for caterpillars.
results.proof_sketch: Its bipartition classes are A={c,w1,w2,w3} and B={u1,u2,u3}. Complementation lets us assume A receives 1,2,3,4 and B receives 5,6,7. Give an A-vertex rank p equal to its label and a B-vertex rank q=8−phi, so q runs through 1,2,3. By the criterion, all six edge rank sums must be 2,...,7. Let r be c's rank. The center-edge sums are r+1,r+2,r+3. If r=1, sum 7 on a leaf edge forces ranks (4,3), after which the largest remaining sum is 3+2=5, not the required 6. If r=4, sum 2 forces (1,1), after which the smallest remaining sum is 2+2=4, not 3. If r=2, sums 2 and 7 force (1,1) and (4,3), leaving 3+2=5 instead of 6. If r=3, sums 2 and 7 similarly leave 2+2=4 instead of 3. All cases are impossible.

results.claim: The checker’s inductive generator contains exactly one representative of every unlabeled tree at each tested order.
results.proof_sketch: Begin with the one-vertex tree. To form the next level, attach a new leaf at every vertex of every current representative. Every larger tree occurs because deleting any leaf gives a tree from the preceding level, and transporting the deleted leaf through an isomorphism recovers one generated attachment. For deduplication, the code of a rooted tree is a parenthesized, lexicographically sorted multiset of its child codes. Induction on size shows equality of these codes is equivalent to rooted isomorphism. An unrooted tree has either one center or a central edge; coding at the unique center, or sorting the two rooted codes obtained by cutting the central edge, therefore gives a complete isomorphism invariant. The implementation distinguishes the two center types and retains one tree per code.

results.claim: For n≥2, in searching for a graceful labeling, it is complete to guess an edge, give its endpoints labels 0 and n−1 in one orientation, and search the remaining labels.
results.proof_sketch: For n≥2, the n−1 distinct positive edge differences available from labels 0,...,n−1 must be all of 1,...,n−1. Difference n−1 can arise only between labels 0 and n−1, so some edge has these endpoints. The complement transformation x↦n−1−x preserves every difference and reverses the orientation; hence one orientation for each possible edge is sufficient.

results.claim: The persisted backtracking and validation procedure is exact: every reported witness is graceful, and its pruning rules cannot remove a possible completion.
results.proof_sketch: Starting from the guessed extreme edge, assigned vertices remain connected. Thus every unassigned boundary vertex has exactly one assigned neighbor; two would create a cycle. The search chooses a boundary vertex and exhausts every unused label whose resulting parent-edge difference is unused. Choice ordering changes no search branch. It prunes only if some boundary edge has no such candidate, or if an unused required difference is realizable on no unresolved edge using currently free labels; either condition is incompatible with any completion. At termination, a separate validator sorts the labels and edge differences and requires exact equality with {0,...,n−1} and {1,...,n−1}, respectively.

The command completed without a failed search or validation assertion, reporting `all_graceful=yes` at every order. All operations use finite integers, tuples, strings, and integer bit masks.

results.claim: Every tree on at most 15 vertices is graceful.
results.proof_sketch: By the generator claim, every such tree is isomorphic to one of the representatives in the completed run. By the validation claim each representative has a graceful labeling. Transporting that labeling along an isomorphism, and adding one to the checker’s 0-based labels, gives the required bijection onto {1,...,n}.

results.claim: Any counterexample to the graceful tree conjecture must have at least 16 vertices and contain a vertex adjacent to at least three non-leaf vertices.
results.proof_sketch: The finite certification excludes orders at most 15, and the caterpillar theorem excludes caterpillars. In any tree with at least three vertices, the set of non-leaves induces a connected subtree: every internal vertex on a path between two non-leaves has its two path neighbors and is therefore also a non-leaf. If every vertex had at most two non-leaf neighbors, this induced connected subtree would have maximum degree at most two and hence would be a path, making the original tree a caterpillar. The contrapositive supplies the asserted local structure.
